title: Streamline ingest: canonical weight index, sharding dialect adapters, and tokenizer boundary contract
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Problem statement:
The model ingestion pipeline currently supports multiple weight file dialects and ad-hoc sharding conventions. Tokenizer loading is tightly coupled into several loader code paths which increases memory pressure and makes validation brittle. This has produced repeated edge-case bugs during large-model uploads, long cold-start times for first inference, and a maintenance burden for onboarding new checkpoint formats.

Goal:
- Introduce a canonical weight index manifest (compact JSON) that normalizes weight metadata across formats and serves as the single source of truth for shard maps and dtype/quantization hints.
- Implement thin sharding-dialect adapters that translate external formats into the canonical index instead of embedding format logic throughout the runtime.
- Split tokenizer handshake into a small, verifiable tokenizer manifest and a runtime tokenizer loader that can be lazy-initialized and validated independently.

Success criteria (measurable):
- New canonical manifest produced for 95% of model uploads within the onboarding tests without format-specific code changes.
- Cold-start model load latency reduced by >= 20% for multi-shard models on p4 instances (measured in CI perf jobs).
- Tokenizer-related memory retained at startup reduced by >= 30% by using lazy tokenizer loader.
- No regressions on compatibility: runtime supports legacy checkpoint formats via adapters for at least 3 months before deprecation warnings.

Design summary:
1) Canonical weight index: a minimal JSON that maps each parameter name to a list of shard entries: {shard_id, byte_range, shape, dtype_hint, quant_profile_ref}. This manifest will be emitted by a new ingestion stage (ingest-normalizer) and stored alongside model metadata in the registry.
2) Sharding-dialect adapters: small translator modules (pluggable) that read format-specific headers (HuggingFace sharded, custom-s3-slices, legacy contiguous files) and emit the canonical index. Adapters run in a short-lived worker and are built to be memory-frugal.
3) Tokenizer manifest + lazy loader: tokenizer files (vocab, merges, tokenizer-config) are summarized in a tokenizer manifest containing a stable checksum, model->tokenizer compatibility assertions, and an initialization hint (eager|lazy). The runtime validates the checksum before accepting the manifest and only fetches/initializes tokenizer artifacts on the first request that requires model tokenization.
4) Backwards compatibility layer: for existing models we ship a compatibility adapter that generates canonical manifests on-demand and stores them as a migration artifact. A migration job will batch-convert high-traffic models first.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (opt-in): merge adapters behind a feature flag ingest.canonical_index=true. Add CI ingestion tests (conformance suite).
- Phase 1 (shadow): enable on a subset of uploads and run shadow manifests in parallel. Collect metrics and run perf comparisons.
- Phase 2 (opt-out conversion): run background migration for top-500 models by traffic; expose conversion status in Console.
- Phase 3 (enforce): after 90 days of stable telemetry and no regressions, flip default and mark older paths deprecated.

Testing & validation:
- Conformance harness to verify adapters produce identical parameter placings for a set of canonical golden models.
- Perf CI to measure cold-start and memory footprint across representative shards and instance types.
- Fuzz tests for malformed shard headers and intentionally truncated downloads.
- End-to-end canaries using a small set of production traffic.

Operational notes:
- Metrics to track: manifest generation time, adapter failure rate, first-byte latency for shard downloads, tokenizer init traces, memory delta at model attach, migration conversion rate.
- Alerts: adapter error rate > 1% for 10m, manifest validation failures > 0.5% for 10m.

Migration risks and mitigations:
- Risk: adapter bug produces incorrect byte_range mapping -> mitigation: conservative validation step (recalculate parameter checksums post-assembly) and independent verifier job.
- Risk: tokenizer lazy-init causes first-request latency spikes -> mitigation: provide an explicit prewarm API for customers and default to eager for low-latency tier models.

Open questions/decisions to make:
- Format for quant_profile_ref (inline vs. pointer to artifact).
- How long to keep compatibility adapters before hard deprecation (propose 90 days).
- Whether to expose canonical manifest in public model catalog API or keep internal-only for now (propose internal-only until stable).

Acceptance criteria for merging the initial implementation:
- Unit and integration tests covering three adapter formats (HF-sharded, contiguous-ckpt, custom-s3-slices).
- CI perf jobs demonstrating the expected cold-start and memory improvements.
- A clear migration dashboard card with conversion progress for customer models.
